text:
mike_infra: Heads-up — noticing a sharp rise in preemptions in the us-west2 preemptible pool. Eviction rate jumped ~20% in last 30m, spill events starting at 17:02 UTC.

tara_sre: saw it too. Prometheus shows a cluster-level eviction spike plus network packet drops on a subset of hosts.

kevin_sre: impact? which workloads?

mike_infra: mostly best-effort batch customers and some low-tier realtime tenants. A few dedicated lanes saw transient latency bumps due to noisy spill. No major host failures.

nina_prod: customer VX-102 reported timeout errors around 17:05 — they’re on low priority. Can we avoid SLO break for mid-tier tenants?

mike_infra: plan proposal: 1) enable soft-spill to nearby region (us-west1) for <30% of queued spot requests 2) warm-reserve a small standby of ondemand GPUs for mid-tier 3) degrade to smaller quantized model variants when routing out-of-region would exceed p99 latency.

tara_sre: agree. We should also throttle fanout to prevent cascading regional bursts. Add token-bucket per-tenant when spilling.

kevin_sre: concrete routing change suggestion: change routing weights dynamically based on recent eviction_rate metric and lane_qps. If eviction_rate > 10% then reduce spot_weight by 50% and increase reserved_weight.

mike_infra: here's a quick config sketch for runtime to implement soft-spill + model degrade (for discussion):

```yaml
routing_policy:
  thresholds:
    eviction_rate: 0.10   # trigger threshold
  actions:
    - name: soft_spill
      to_region: us-west1
      max_percent: 30
      per_tenant_token_bucket: 50
    - name: variant_degrade
      target_variant: gpt-cpu-q4_0
      max_qps: 200
    - name: reserve_warm_pool
      warm_count: 6
      for_tiers: [mid,high]
```

nina_prod: that looks reasonable. How do we pick which tenants get warm pool access? priority based on spend + recent error budget?

tara_sre: yes, use tenant_tier + rolling_error_budget. Also consider a decaying score so someone who used warm pool for a short burst doesn't keep it.

kevin_sre: operational concerns: cross-region KV cache invalidation for chat sessions when spilling to us-west1. We should only spill stateless inference or ensure KV prefix routing stays local.

mike_infra: good call. Split policy: stateful sessions (kv_hits > 0) must stay in-region or be degraded to smaller model that fits local capacity. Stateless requests are eligible for full spill.

nina_prod: customer comms? will notify VX-102 that we may move some requests temporarily. Keep it minimal.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1298, severity: advisory — preemptible eviction surge in us-west2. Assigned: mike_infra.

tara_sre: can we add jittered retry on client side for mid-tier so we avoid synchronized retry storms? 200-500ms jitter + exponential backoff.

mike_infra: yes adding to client SDK backlog. Also we should instrument per-variant quality regression check when we auto-degrade to quantized model — run a small eval set to detect big quality drop and fallback if needed.

kevin_sre: how about cost guardrails? spilling to ondemand/reserved wastes spot savings. Suggest a dynamic budget: only use warm pool if expected cost delta per-tenant < monthly_threshold and only for error-critical tenants.

mike_infra: agreed. Add a cost-window estimator that estimates tokens * unit_cost_by_variant across the spill window. If projected extra spend > tenant_budget then prefer variant_degrade over region_spill.

tara_sre: I'll PR a controller that watches eviction_rate and flips routing weights + enforces per-tenant token buckets. Need someone to review the degrade/quality check logic.

nina_prod: I'll own the quality check harness and a small canary eval set for key tenants.

kevin_sre: I'll add the KV safety rules and ensure traffic labeled 'stateful' is excluded from cross-region spill.

mike_infra: timeline?

tara_sre: can get a basic controller patch today, deploy to staging tomorrow, and a limited rollout to prod canary (10% of mid-tier) Friday.

mike_infra: OK. For now I’m going to lower spot_weight and enable token buckets to throttle spill. Will monitor metrics.

ops-bot: Deployment started: routing-controller v0.9.3 -> staging.

mike_infra: monitoring: eviction_rate coming down to baseline, p95 latency recovering. Will keep thread updated.

nina_prod: thanks team. Please post any customer-impacting updates here.
